package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after a change in domain ownership. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically deployed to all dependent sites and packages.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the script is loaded by the browser)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Detects if the visitor is using a mobile device and, if so, redirects them to a scam website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user-agent sniffing and forcibly redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled site, which is not expected behavior for a polyfill library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill library should only provide JavaScript compatibility shims for older browsers, not perform user redirection or interact with the DOM in this way.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User-agent detection and redirection can be legitimate in some web applications for mobile optimization, but never in a third-party polyfill library.
key_indicators: Redirection to non-affiliated, potentially malicious domains
Injected into a widely used third-party library

attack_chain.action: Website or npm package includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io (e.g., <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser loads and executes the JavaScript from the CDN

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript code is delivered by the compromised CDN endpoint
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the website visitor's browser

attack_chain.action: Malicious code checks if the visitor is on a mobile device and redirects them to a scam site if so
attack_chain.leads_to: User is sent to a phishing or scam landing page, enabling further attacks (e.g., credential theft, malware delivery)

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript performing user-agent sniffing and redirection
Unexpected window.location.href assignments in polyfill or utility libraries
Polyfill scripts containing code unrelated to browser compatibility
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in script tags or npm package source code
Polyfill JavaScript files with obfuscated or appended redirect logic
network_indicators: Redirections to known scam or phishing domains from pages loading polyfill.io scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for script tags or dependencies referencing cdn.polyfill.io in web applications and npm packages. Monitor loaded JavaScript for unexpected behaviors such as user-agent sniffing and window.location redirects. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to block or report scripts from untrusted sources. Employ Subresource Integrity (SRI) to ensure third-party scripts have not been tampered with. Flag any polyfill or utility library that performs DOM redirection or network requests to suspicious domains.
